result: yR7 photoreceptors expressing Dpr11 specifically connect to yDm8 amacrine neurons expressing DIP-γ, while pR7 photoreceptors connect to pDm8 neurons lacking DIP-γ. The ratio of yDm8:pDm8 (60:40) matches the ratio of yR7:pR7 (65:35) in the retina.
evaluation: Claims C1-C4, C38-C41, C50-C51, C57-C58, C61-C62, and C104 collectively demonstrate specific connectivity patterns between R7 subtypes and Dm8 subtypes. Single-cell flipout experiments (C57-C58, C61), immunohistochemistry (C62), and cell counting (C51) provide converging evidence. The matching ratios (C50-C51) support the biological significance of this organization.

result: Analysis of EM reconstruction reveals separate 'yellow' and 'pale' circuits for UV wavelength discrimination. yR7 and yDm8 preferentially synapse onto Tm5a (which expresses DIP-γ), while pR7 and pDm8 synapse onto Tm5b (which does not express DIP-γ).
evaluation: Claims C42-C44, C66-C78, C166-C167 are supported by detailed analysis of the EM reconstruction (Figure 3). The identification of R7 subtypes based on Tm5a/b connectivity (C68-C73) and the demonstration of parallel specificity in Dm8→Tm5 connections (C76-C78) provide strong evidence for distinct circuits. The expression of DIP-γ in Tm5a but not Tm5b (C74) supports the molecular basis for circuit specificity.

result: DIP-γ and Dpr11 are required for normal morphogenesis of yDm8 distal dendrites (sprigs). Mutants show significantly decreased sprig diameter and increased frequency of two-home column neurons, though sprig height and percentage of yR7 columns contacted remain largely unaffected.
evaluation: Claims C45-C46, C54-C55, C81-C91, C144-C145, C147-C148 demonstrate morphological defects in mutants through quantitative analysis of flipout clones (Figure 5) and ExM imaging (Figure 6). The EM reconstruction data (C147-C148) supports the functional significance of sprig morphology for synapse distribution. Statistical significance is shown for sprig diameter changes (C85), and the ExM-EM comparison (C91) validates the imaging approaches.

result: yDm8 neurons are generated in excess during development and compete for yR7 partners. Dpr11-DIP-γ interactions are required for yDm8 survival, with ~50-60% of yDm8 dying in DIP-γ or dpr11 mutants. This selection mechanism ensures matching ratios of yDm8:pDm8 and yR7:pR7.
evaluation: Claims C6-C7, C47-C49, C97-C107, C128-C130 are supported by developmental time course experiments (Figure 8A), cell counting in mutants (Figure 7), and DIAP rescue experiments. The ~50% loss in single mutants (C97-C98), similar phenotype in double mutants (C99-C100), partial rescue with DIP-γ transgene (C101), and complete rescue with DIAP (C130) provide strong evidence for a survival signaling mechanism. The developmental timing data (C128-C129) establishes when cell death occurs.

result: yR7 and yDm8 meet and select each other in the incipient layer by 15-20 hr APF, prior to synaptogenesis. Dpr11 is expressed in R7 by 15 hr APF, DIP-γ is expressed in Dm8 by 18-20 hr APF, and yDm8 cell death in mutants begins between 15-25 hr APF.
evaluation: Claims C119-C125, C133 establish the developmental timeline through reporter expression analysis (C119-C120, Figure 8F-G) and cell death timing (C125, Figure 8A). The inference that selection occurs by 15-20 hr APF (C123-C124) is well-supported by the convergence of Dpr11 expression, DIP-γ expression, and R7 growth cone positioning data. The independence from synaptogenesis (C133) is supported by the timing difference (selection before 25 hr APF vs. synaptogenesis after 60 hr APF).

result: Dpr11-DIP-γ interactions allow yDm8 to select yR7 as appropriate partners. yDm8 and pDm8 do not normally compete, but can be forced to compete by manipulating R7 subtype fate. When all R7 express Dpr11 or are converted to yR7, more yDm8 survive and almost all pDm8 die.
evaluation: Claims C8-C10, C108-C114, C139-C140 are supported by gain-of-function experiments (Figure 9). The lack of competition in wild-type is demonstrated by unchanged pDm8 numbers when yDm8 are rescued with DIAP (C111). Forced competition is shown by pDm8 death when all R7 express Dpr11 (C113, C139-C140) and yDm8 death when all R7 are converted to pR7 (C114). The sufficiency of Dpr11 expression for yDm8 selection (C140) is clearly demonstrated.

result: pDm8 neurons are preferentially selected by pR7 PRs through unknown molecular mechanisms, and pR7 are required for pDm8 survival. pDm8 are unable to effectively fill vacant yR7 slots, with only ~30 additional pDm8 surviving despite ~180 vacant yR7 slots in ssGOF, DIP-γ mutants.
evaluation: Claims C115-C118, C141-C143 demonstrate pDm8 selection mechanisms and limitations. The inability of pDm8 to fill yR7 slots (C117-C118) is quantitatively demonstrated. The lack of mistargeting in dpr11 mutants (C141) is explained by pR7 occupancy. The suggestion of a second support mechanism (C142-C143) is reasonable speculation based on the differential loss in sev vs. DIP-γ/dpr11 mutants, though this remains to be tested.

result: Each Dm8 arbor contacts 12-16 medulla columns, with most synapses made in the home column. The distal dendritic projection (sprig) extends from M6 to M4 and tiles the medulla. yDm8 show a ~15% higher bias for contacting yR7 columns compared to pDm8.
evaluation: Claims C52-C56, C63-C65 describe Dm8 arbor organization through EM reconstruction and single-cell analysis. The 12-16 column contact range (C52) and home column preference (C53) are well-established from cited literature and confirmed here. The sprig morphology (C54-C55) and tiling pattern (C56) are demonstrated through imaging. The yDm8 bias for yR7 (C64) is statistically significant, though the total number of R7 contacted is similar (C63).

result: Two-home column yDm8 occur at ~6% frequency in wild-type and ~4.5-fold higher frequency in DIP-γ mutants. All two-home column yDm8 have both sprigs on yR7 columns.
evaluation: Claims C59-C60, C87 document the frequency and specificity of two-home column neurons through single-cell flipout experiments. The increased frequency in DIP-γ mutants (C87, Figure 5G) suggests a compensatory response to loss of survival signals. The maintenance of yR7 specificity in two-home column neurons (C60) supports the robustness of the selection mechanism.

result: R7 is histaminergic and inhibits both Dm8 and Tm5a/b through polyadic synapses. Dm8 is glutamatergic while Tm5a/b are cholinergic. This suggests yR7 input might inhibit Tm5a through both direct and indirect (via yDm8) mechanisms.
evaluation: Claims C79-C80, C92-C96 describe the neurotransmitter identities and synaptic organization. The histaminergic nature of R7 and inhibitory function (C92) is supported by cited literature and EM data showing polyadic synapses (C80). The neurotransmitter identities of Dm8 and Tm5 (C93-C94) are from cited sources. The inference about dual inhibition mechanisms (C95-C96) is reasonable based on the circuit architecture.

result: Widespread cell death occurs in the medullary cortex during normal development in two phases, with the first phase spanning 0-48 hr APF and peaking at 24 hr APF. The yDm8 that die in wild-type are inferred to be those in excess of the number that can be selected by yR7.
evaluation: Claims C126-C127 cite established developmental biology (Togane et al., 2012). Claims C131-C132 are reasonable inferences based on the observation that more yDm8 survive when more R7 express Dpr11 (demonstrated in gain-of-function experiments). The inference is logical but indirect, as the specific identity of dying cells in wild-type is not directly demonstrated.

result: DIP-α-expressing Dm4 neurons show similar developmental excess and DIP-Dpr-dependent survival as yDm8. However, not all DIP-γ-expressing neurons require it for survival, as lobula plate tangential cells expressing DIP-γ do not die in DIP-γ mutants.
evaluation: Claims C134-C136 cite previous work (Xu et al., 2018) establishing parallel mechanisms in Dm4 neurons. Claims C137-C138 are based on unpublished observations but provide important context about the specificity of DIP-γ function. The comparison strengthens the interpretation that DIP-Dpr interactions can have context-dependent roles.

result: The effects of Dpr11 and DIP-γ on yDm8 sprig morphology may involve a different pathway from cell death. An 'overshoot' phenotype with Brp-short marker is observed in dpr11 mutants, but its interpretation is unclear as it doesn't correspond to endogenous Brp distribution changes.
evaluation: Claims C149-C150 are reasonable inferences but remain speculative. The overshoot phenotype (C151-C154) shows conflicting results between different markers (Brp-short vs. endogenous Brp) and genotypes (dpr11Mi>GFP/Df vs. dpr11CRISPR). The authors appropriately note the unclear interpretation (C154), indicating this requires further investigation. The pathway distinction (C149) is inferred from timing but not directly tested.

result: The absorption spectra of Rh4 and Rh3 extensively overlap, making learned color discrimination unlikely. However, the existence of separate y and p circuits suggests flies use them for UV wavelength discrimination, with longer-wave UV preferentially inhibiting Tm5a and shorter-wave UV preferentially inhibiting Tm5b.
evaluation: Claims C162-C165, C171-C174, C178 present a model for UV wavelength discrimination based on circuit architecture. The spectral overlap (C162) is demonstrated, and the inference about discrimination difficulty (C163) is reasonable. However, the proposed mechanism (C171-C173) is speculative and not directly tested. The model (C174) requires identification of downstream neurons that read Tm5a:Tm5b ratios, which is not provided. This represents a plausible hypothesis requiring experimental validation.

result: The Drosophila visual system consists of ~750 ommatidia, each with 8 photoreceptors expressing different rhodopsins. Outer PRs (R1-R6) are used for motion detection, while inner PRs (R7 and R8) transmit chromatic information. The system is organized retinotopically with ~65% yellow and ~35% pale ommatidia.
evaluation: Claims C24-C37 provide established background on Drosophila visual system anatomy and function. These are well-documented facts from the literature (cited appropriately) and serve as necessary context for the experimental work. The behavioral capabilities (C36-C37) are also well-established from cited sources.

result: The Drosophila genome encodes ~1000 CSPs, with each neuronal type expressing >250 CSP genes. The Dpr-ome consists of 21 Dpr and 11 DIP proteins with binding affinities of 1-200 μM. DIPs and Dprs have diverse functions in neural development including synapse formation, axon guidance, and cell survival.
evaluation: Claims C11-C23 provide essential background on DIPs and Dprs from cited literature. These establish the molecular context for the current study and document the known functions of these protein families. All claims are appropriately cited and provide necessary foundation for interpreting the experimental results.

result: Tm5a/b/c are output neurons that receive input from R7, R8, and Dm8 and project to the lobula. Four Tm neuron classes (Tm5a/b/c and Tm20) contribute to blue-green discrimination. Tm5c is required for innate UV preference, with no y vs. p specificity in connections to Tm5c.
evaluation: Claims C155-C161, C168-C170, C175-C177 describe Tm5 neuron properties and functions from cited literature and EM reconstruction analysis. The lack of y/p specificity for Tm5c (C170) is demonstrated in the EM data. The behavioral roles (C160-C161, C169, C177) are from cited sources. The hypotheses about Tm5 function (C158-C159) are appropriately presented as speculation.
